title: Original D4 chessboard representation: global balance versus local domino partner shortage
subject: TEST
scope_summary: Wholly original 6x6 domino board where 15 black and 15 white squares remain but no domino tiling exists due to a local neighbor shortage; same-color hole transfer admits a full tiling.

supports_claims: Each domino spans two orthogonally adjacent cells of opposite checkerboard colors.

conventions.statement: Each 1x2 domino covers two orthogonally adjacent surviving squares.
A square (r,c) is black if r+c is even, white otherwise; the top-left is black.
Removed holes are not covered and cannot be used by a domino.
Each surviving square may belong to exactly one domino.

capabilities.action: Choose a stronger adjacency-graph representation when global chessboard color counts are inconclusive, and prove a local shortage or build a full domino matching.
capabilities.success_criterion: Independently show a balanced six-hole 6x6 board lacks a domino cover because three black cells have only two distinct white neighbors, then construct 15 pairs when one hole relocates.

exit_task.prompt: Remove the top-left and bottom-right corner squares of a 4x4 checkerboard. Decide if domino tiling is possible using only the necessary color-count test.

answer.summary: No: both removed corners are black, leaving six black and eight white squares.
reasoning: The complete 4x4 has eight squares of each color.
Cells (r1,c1) and (r4,c4) have the same even coordinate parity and are both black.
Removing both leaves six black and eight white squares, impossible for dominoes pairing one of each.
answer.check: Seven dominoes would require seven of each color, contradicting 6:8.

boundary_test.prompt: A 4x4 board loses (r1,c2),(r2,c1),(r3,c3),(r4,c4); color totals still match. Why is top-left (r1,c1) impossible to pair? If r1c2 is restored, what claim remains unproved?
boundary_test.answer: Both neighbors of r1c1 were removed; it cannot be covered. Restoring r1c2 removes this simple obstruction but is not itself a full-board tiling proof.
boundary_test.confirms: Balanced totals plus removal of one local obstruction do not certify a complete tiling.

questions.stem: For an unbroken 2×3 checkerboard, place one vertical domino in each column. Explain why each domino covers opposite colors and show that all six cells are covered.
conditions: One 1×2 domino covers adjacent horizontal or vertical squares.
Every surviving square is used once.

answer.summary: Three vertical dominoes exactly cover three black and three white squares.
reasoning: The 2×3 grid has three black and three white squares.
Vertical pairs (r1c1,r2c1),(r1c2,r2c2),(r1c3,r2c3) cover all cells exactly once.
Every vertical domino spans one black and one white square.
answer.check: Each of six coordinates appears exactly once in the three pairs.

questions.stem: A 6×6 checkerboard has (r1,c1) black. Remove exactly six cells: (r1,c4), (r2,c3), (r3,c2), (r3,c3), (r4,c6), (r5,c1). You may place 1×2 dominoes only on two full-edge adjacent surviving cells; each surviving cell must be covered once, without overlap. A classmate sees equal black and white totals and concludes a complete tiling MUST exist. For this particular board, decide whether complete tiling exists. Choose and justify a stronger representation if needed: an allowed-pair graph, a decisive local obstruction, or a complete constructive tiling. Explain why your evidence settles the case; a global color total by itself is not an answer.
conditions: Rows and columns from 1 through 6, top-left black.
Exactly the six named coordinates are removed.
All other grid cells are available.
Dominoes are horizontal or vertical, never diagonal.
Dominoes may not overlap or reuse any cell.

answer.summary: No tiling although 15 black and 15 white cells remain: three black cells (r1c1,r2c2,r1c3) can use only two white neighbors (r2c1,r1c2).
reasoning: The three removed black cells are (r3,c3),(r4,c6),(r5,c1), and three removed white cells are (r1,c4),(r2,c3),(r3,c2): remaining black:white is 15:15.
Represent possible dominoes by a bipartite adjacency graph between surviving opposite-color neighbors.
Choose S={(r1,c1),(r2,c2),(r1,c3)} of three black squares. Their only surviving neighboring white squares are N(S)={(r2,c1),(r1,c2)}.
Every black square of S requires a DIFFERENT white partner. Three distinct partners cannot be drawn from two white squares.
Therefore a full domino tiling is impossible despite global balance.

reasoning_route.action: Translate removed coordinates into a global checkerboard count.
reasoning_route.output: 15 black and 15 white remain, not decisive.

reasoning_route.action: Represent possible dominoes as edges of a bipartite graph.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Only orthogonally adjacent surviving squares can be paired.
Three distinct black cells need three distinct white partners but only two exist.
reasoning_route.output: Local shortage proves no full tiling.

reasoning_route.action: Independently list every legal neighbor of those three black cells.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Other candidates are holes or outside grid.

answer.check: r1c1 has neighbors r1c2,r2c1; r2c2 has r1c2,r2c1 (r2c3,r3c2 removed); r1c3 has r1c2 (r1c4,r2c3 removed).

scaffolds.text: Start with one domino: which two checkerboard colors does it cover? Is equality of totals necessary or sufficient?
A color tally does not describe WHICH squares can pair. Try a graph with an edge for every legal neighboring pair.
Only AFTER recording an attempt: find a small group of same-color squares that must each have a DIFFERENT opposite-color partner. Compare the group size to the number of distinct possible neighbors.

questions.stem: The arrangement CHANGES: remove the second table along the TOP row of the 4×4 border. The formerly sealed 2×2 courtyard now connects to the outside through the one-cell opening. All other table positions are unchanged. The same one-chair-per-EXTERIOR-ACCESSIBLE-table-side rule applies; sides along the opening are accessible if a path of empty cells from outside reaches them. Rebuild your variables and model for the NEW geometry and determine exactly how many chair sites are available. Explain why simply subtracting one table's four original sides from the former 16-chair result is invalid.
conditions: Start with the 4×4 border-ring table placement of Core2A.
Remove top row, second column table (not a corner).
The empty corridor now connects the former enclosed center to exterior via orthogonally adjacent empty cells.
All unshared table sides adjacent to exterior-connected space are accessible.
One chair per such unit side; shared contacts still cannot hold chairs.

answer.summary: The open layout has n=11,e=10,c=0, so 24 outside-accessible chair sites.
reasoning: Removing the top row second column leaves eleven occupied unit-table cells.
In the original 12-cell ring that removed noncorner table touched exactly two other border tables, so removing it eliminates two contacts: e falls from12 to10.
The missing top position opens a one-cell path from exterior to all formerly enclosed empty central cells; there is no sealed cavity, so c=0.
The new accessible chair count is A=4×11−2×10−0=24.

Direct exterior-connected edge tracing shows twenty-four reachable unshared table sides. The count increases from16 despite removing a table, because former inner courtyard edges become accessible; 16−4 is not a valid model.

reasoning_route.action: Remodel the 4×4 shape with its top noncorner table absent.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Original twelve occupied tables minus one leaves n11.

reasoning_route.action: Recount shared contacts after removing the table and its two full-edge joins.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The removed noncorner top table formerly met its two horizontal neighbors.

reasoning_route.action: Classify courtyard void as exterior-connected through the new top-row opening; update inaccessible sides.
reasoning_route.why_valid: An orthogonal path of vacant cells now reaches the courtyard from outside.

reasoning_route.action: Evaluate A=4n−2e−c and cross-check exposed accessible boundary.
reasoning_route.why_valid: 44−20=24; every now-exposed side borders exterior-connected empty space.

answer.check: Direct exterior flood fill yields 24 side interfaces. It is larger than the closed-ring 16 because opening the courtyard makes formerly inaccessible inner edges reachable.
